newsitem.title: USA: Federated Stores to prepay debt, record charge.
newsitem.headline: Federated Stores to prepay debt, record charge.

text.p: Federated Department Stores Inc. said Monday it has agreed to prepay $498.4 million of mortgage debt to Prudential Insurance Co.
Federated, which operates Bloomingdale's, Macy's, Burdines and other stores, also said it plans to replace its $2.5 billion secured bank credit agreement with a $2 billion unsecured bank loan.

The company said the transactions allow it to lower its total interest expense, eliminate much of its secured debt and substantially extend the maturities of the debt, all which will improve its financial flexibility.

"The company's operating results and our recent credit rating upgrade, coupled with the excellent conditions in the credit markets, make this an opportune time for us to refinance a large portion of our debt," said Federated Chairman James Zimmerman.

The company said the debt plans will result in an extraordinary charge to be reported in the current quarter of $60 million to $65 million, relating to the premium being paid for the mortgage prepayment and the write-off of deferred financing charges on the refinanced debt.
As a result of these transactions, the company expects to save $15 million to $20 million in annual interest expense.
Federated said the transaction is expected to be financed by long-term unsecured notes issued through an underwriting group led by Goldman Sachs.
